clusters.rationale: All four items implement the same v3 ladder closure tool. Items 149 and 150 explicitly bundle the full ladder (sig_1 + sig_2/3 + sig_4), citing the same W9a-97 / W9a-98 / W9a-100 inputs. Items 116 (HOOK-WIRING) and 128 (PLAN-PRU-REMEDIATION) are subcomponents independently pre-registered by the same origin (mack): 128 is the sig_1 tagging step (89 unpinned gates -> D_PRU_raw=0) and 116 is the sig_3/sig_4 step (settings.json PostToolUse + Stop matchers per s84-w9a-98-settings-diff.md, plus R3 YAML normalization of 87 non-compliant gates). Same infrastructure, same W9a carry-forward inputs, same output (ladder -> CLOSED). Conservative merge is justified: these are not distinct tools but the same ladder remediated via its constituent signals.

singletons.title: Plan-layer PRDR consistency audit tool (hypothesis IMPLIES or CONTRADICTS each cross-check)
singletons.rationale: New tool at plan-write time that audits hypothesis -> cross-check logical consistency (IMPLIES/CONTRADICTS semantics over plan text). Distinct from PLAN-PRU-REMEDIATION (raw_index 128), which is execution-time remediation of unpinned machinery parameters via `# (local)` tagging or canonical_constants.py promotion. PRDR at plan-write time != PRU cardinality audit at execution time (per bucket instruction's key distinction). Cites W9a-97 PRU infrastructure as leverage, not as the same tool. Conservative merge rule requires treating these as separate tools.
